system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}

Trial: VICTORION-2P NCT05030428 - Study of Inclisiran to Prevent Cardiovascular (CV) Events in Participants With Established Cardiovascular Disease
Investigational drug: inclisiran sodium
Document: Efficacy, Safety, and Pharmacokinetics of Inclisiran in Japanese Patients: Results from ORION-15. (journal, published 2024-01-14, source pmcid:PMC11150722)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
1 2 3 4 5 6 Aim: To evaluate the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics (PK) of inclisiran in Japanese patients with high cardiovascular risk and elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C). Methods: ORION-15 was a phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial. Patients with hypercholesterolemia, including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH), were randomized to inclisiran sodium 100, 200, or 300 mg, or placebo and dosed subcutaneously on Days 1, 90, and 270. The primary endpoint was the percentage change from baseline to Day 180 to demonstrate the superiority of inclisiran vs. placebo. Patients who consented to the PK substudy had additional study procedures for blood collection and safety assessment. Results: Overall, 312 patients (mean age, 63.6 years; male, 74.4%; baseline LDL-C, 114.0 mg/dL) were randomized. Baseline characteristics were well balanced among the groups. At Day 180, inclisiran at all doses demonstrated significant LDL-C and proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) reductions (p＜0.0001 for both), which showed a dose–response relationship. The greatest reductions (LDL-C, 65.3%; PCSK9, 79.2%) were with inclisiran sodium 300 mg. At Day 180, ＞86% of the patients receiving inclisiran achieved the Japan Atherosclerosis Society 2017 lipid management targets compared to 8.9% for placebo. The mean (SD) plasma half-life for inclisiran was 6.8 (2.0)–7.6 (0.8) h. The incidence of adverse events with inclisiran was similar to that with placebo. Conclusion: Inclisiran sodium 100, 200, and 300 mg demonstrated clinically meaningful and statistically significant LDL-C and PCSK9 reductions at Day 180, which were consistent over 12 months. Inclisiran was effective and well tolerated in Japanese patients with hypercholesterolemia, including HeFH. Introduction According to the World Health Organization, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) is the leading cause of death worldwide 1) . In 2019, heart disease accounted for 15% of all deaths reported in Japan and the national medical expense was estimated to be 2 trillion yen (~18.6 billion US dollars) 2) . Elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is a major risk factor for the development of ASCVD 3 - 5) . In Japan, the prevalence of ASCVD and the associated healthcare burden have increased in recent years. Adoption of a westernized lifestyle combined with an aging population in Japan further increases the risk of ASCVD 6 , 7) . Global studie
...
s have demonstrated that lowering LDL-C levels is directly proportional to a reduction in cardiovascular (CV) risk 8 , 9) . LDL-C-modifying therapies reduce the risk of CV events and mortality by slowing the progression of ASCVD, thus leading to improved CV outcomes 10 , 11) . The Japan Atherosclerosis Society (JAS) Guidelines for Prevention of Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Diseases 2017/2022 recommend an LDL-C target based on an individual patient’s CV risk 12 , 13) . To reduce CV disease risk, the JAS Guidelines 2022 recommend statins as a first-line therapy to lower LDL-C and ezetimibe or proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitors (PCSK9i) in case of insufficient efficacy with statins 13) . It is observed that only 25.4% of patients with high-risk secondary prevention (LDL-C goal ＜70 mg/dL), 60.6% of those with secondary prevention (LDL-C goal ＜100 mg/dL), and 65.5% of those with high-risk primary prevention (LDL-C goal ＜120 mg/dL) attain the recommended levels of LDL-C 14) . The results from an observational study involving patients with FH from Japan reported that only 12.3% of patients without coronary artery disease (CAD) attained LDL-C levels of ＜100 mg/dL and only 1.8% patients with CAD achieved target levels of ＜70 mg/dL 15) . Consequently, the LDL-C goal attainment rate in Japan is far from optimal and ~30% of high-risk patients fail to adhere to the prescribed lipid-modifying therapies (LMTs), including combination therapies 16 , 17) . Inclisiran is a first-in-class small-interfering ribonucleic acid (siRNA) therapy approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration (US FDA) and the European Medicines Agency (EMA) and approved in over 80 countries for the treatment of adults with heterozygous FH (HeFH) or primary hyperlipidemia who require additional lowering of LDL-C, as an adjunct to diet and statin therapy 19 , 20) . Data from pivotal trials with inclisiran have shown that twice-yearly inclisiran sodium 300 mg effectively prevents hepatic PCSK9 production, resulting in consistent and long-term LDL-C reduction 21 - 26) . Aim ORION-15 (NCT04666298) is the first study to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics (PK) of inclisiran in Japanese patients with high CV risk (hypercholesterolemia, including HeFH) and elevated LDL-C. The primary objective of the study was to demonstrate the superiority of inclisiran in reducing LDL-C levels at different doses (inclisiran sodium 100, 200, and 300 mg) compared to placebo at Day 180. Methods Study Design and Patients ORION-15 is a phase 2, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind study comprising a screening period of up to 14 days and a 12-month double-blinded treatment period. Study design of ORION-15 n, number of patients.Among the 32 patients enrolled in the PK substudy, data from 24 patients from the inclisiran treatment groups (eight from each group) were analyzed for PK results. n, number of patients. Among the 32 patients enrolled in the PK substudy, data from 24 patients from the inclisiran treatment groups (eight from each group) were analyzed for PK results. This study included adult Japanese patients (≥ 20 years of age) with a history of CAD or categorized as high risk (diabetes, chronic kidney disease, noncardiogenic cerebral infarction, peripheral arterial disease, or a combination of other risk factors and categorized in “high risk” as assessed by the Suita Score) by the JAS 2017 Guidelines or with HeFH and LDL-C levels higher than the target value defined by JAS 2017 12) . Patients were excluded if they were diagnosed with homozygous FH, were treated within 90 days of screening with monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) directed toward PCSK9, or had any major adverse CV event within 3 months prior to randomization. Randomization and Masking Randomization was stratified by LDL-C at the screening visit (≥ 130 or ＜130 mg/dL), use of statins or other LMTs at baseline, and PK substudy participation. Otherwise, the ratio was 1:2:2:1 for the inclisiran sodium 100, 200, or 300 mg, and placebo groups. Procedures, Treatment Compliance, and Study Duration Inclisiran sodium 100, 200, or 300 mg (equivalent to 94.5, 189, or 284 mg inclisiran, respectively) and placebo were administered as a subcutaneous injection on Days 1, 90, and 270. After Day 180, investigators were notified by the central laboratory in case an LDL-C value had increased by more than 50% or 30 mg/dL compared with the value at baseline. LMTs could be changed after Day 180. mAbs for PCSK9 and LDL-C apheresis treatment were prohibited throughout the study period. The expected duration of patients’ involvement in the study was ~374 days, including the screening period and the follow-up period up to Day 360. Outcomes The primary endpoint of the ORION-15 trial was the percentage change in LDL-C from baseline at Day 180. The key secondary endpoints included the percentage change in PCSK9 and absolute change in LDL-C at Day 180 from baseline. Other secondary endpoints included the proportion of patients at Day 180 who attained the lipid control target prespecified by the JAS 2017 12) (LDL-C ＜70 mg/dL: patients with a history of CAD with additional risk factors such as FH, acute coronary syndrome, or diabetes complicated by other risk factors like noncardiogenic cerebral infarction, peripheral artery disease (PAD), chronic kidney disease, metabolic syndrome, overlap of major risk factors, and smoking; LDL-C ＜100 mg/dL: patients with a history of CAD without additional risk factors or patients with FH without a CAD history; and LDL-C ＜120 mg/dL: patients categorized as high risk) and JAS 2022 13) Guidelines (LDL-C ＜70 mg/dL: patients with a history of CAD or atherothrombotic cerebral infarction with additional risk factors such as acute coronary syndrome, FH, diabetes, and CAD complicated by atherothrombotic cerebral infarction; serum LDL-C ＜100 mg/dL: patients with a history of CAD or atherothrombotic cerebral infarction without additional risk factors, patients with FH without a CAD or atherothrombotic cerebral infarction history, and patients without CAD or atherothrombotic cerebral infarction with diabetes complicated by other risk factors such as PAD, microangiopathy, and smoking; and serum LDL-C ＜120 mg/dL: patients categorized as high risk by the JAS 2022 Guideline, i.e., those with diabetes, CKD, PAD, or a combination of other risk factors and categorized in “high risk” as assessed by the Hisayama-cho Score; attainment of the JAS 2022 lipid control target was as a posthoc analysis of the study); the number of patients reaching on-treatment LDL-C levels of ＜25, ＜50, ＜70, and ＜100 mg/dL up to Day 180; the proportion of patients with ≥ 50% LDL-C reduction from baseline up to Day 180; the percentage change in LDL-C, PCSK9, other lipids, lipoproteins, and apolipoproteins from baseline up to Day 180; the incidence and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) and their association with the study drug; and measurement of antidrug antibodies (ADAs) at baseline and at Days 30, 90, 180, 270, and 360. The exploratory endpoints included the changes from baseline in LDL-C, PCSK9, and other lipids after Day 180 and up to Day 360, as well as responder analysis (the number of patients reaching LDL-C levels of ＜25, ＜50, ＜70, and ＜100 mg/dL and reaching the lipid control target prespecified by JAS 2017 12) and JAS 2022 13) , and the proportion of patients with ≥ 50% LDL-C reduction) from baseline after Day 180 up to Day 360. Sample Size Calculation Assuming a within-treatment-group standard deviation (SD) of 20% for the percentage change from baseline in LDL-C, a sample size of 308 patients was determined to provide ＞90% power for a between-treatment difference of 30% at a one-sided significance level of 0.025. Approximately 8 patients from each treatment group (for a total of approximately 32 patients) were planned to be enrolled in a PK substudy. Mixed models for repeated measures analysis was used for the primary endpoint and key secondary endpoints, based on which the adjusted mean and 95% confidence interval (CI) for the percentage changes within each treatment, the adjusted mean differences and 95% CIs for between-treatment (inclisiran groups vs. placebo), and p-values are reported. The Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) version 25.1 was used for the coding of the adverse events (AEs). A total of 312 patients with hypercholesterolemia, including HeFH, were randomized following an up to 14-day screening period (55 patients in the inclisiran sodium 100 mg group, 101 patients in the 200 mg group, 99 patients in the 300 mg group, and 57 patients in the placebo group). The median duration of treatment exposure over the follow-up duration of 360 days was 357 days in all of the inclisiran groups and 358 days in the placebo group. A total of 32 patients (8 from each of the treatment groups) who consented were enrolled in the PK substudy. The mean baseline LDL-C (SD) was 114.0 (35.72) mg/dL and the mean baseline PCSK9 (SD) was 412.7 (115.95) ng/mL in the total patient population. A total of eight patients (one patient in the inclisiran sodium 200 mg group, four patients in the inclisiran sodium 300 mg group, and three patients in the placebo group) newly started or changed LMT after Day 180. Inclisiran sodium 300 mg N = 99 Placebo N = 57 | Placebo N = 57 Total N = 312 | LDL-C, mg/dL, mean (SD) | 113.4 (33.14) | 116.6 (39.35) | 112.2 (35.50) | 113.1 (32.23) | 114.0 (35.72) | At Day 180, inclisiran sodium 100, 200, and 300 mg demonstrated significant reductions in LDL-C. The primary endpoints of the placebo-adjusted percentage change in LDL-C from baseline to Day 180 were −56.6% (95% CI: −64.2%, −49.0%; p＜0.0001), −60.9% (95% CI: −67.6%, −54.3%; p＜0.0001), and −65.3% (95% CI: −72.0%, −58.6%; p＜0.0001) for inclisiran sodium 100, 200, and 300 mg, respectively ( Supplementary Table 1 ) . The LDL-C reductions were observed from Day 14 and maintained over the entire study duration of approximately 12 months. The response showed dose dependency, and the greatest percentage reduction in LDL-C was observed in the 300 mg dose of inclisiran at any visit up to Day 360 ( Fig.2 ) . The variability in the percentage change in LDL-C from baseline to Day 180 among patients is presented in a waterfall plot ( Supplementary Fig.3 ) .
